text:
anika: Heads up  Helios-12B int4 microquant run shows 3.1x token-cost reduction vs int8 but we see a 9.2% drop on the citation/attribution slice in our 1k-long QA bench. Thoughts?
josh: Oof that's larger than expected. Is the regression uniform or concentrated on named-entity dense prompts?
maya: Mostly entity-dense and multi-retrieval prompts where the model needs to cite sources across turns. Short prompts (<200 tokens) look fine.
li: Any difference with prompt-engineered anchors / system messages? Quant noise might disrupt attention head dynamics for cross-turn grounding.
carla: I pulled logits diffs for a failure case. After the retrieval insertion, top-3 token probs shift, and the model prefers plausible-sounding but incorrect citations.
infra-bot: perf-alert: Helios-12B-int4 canary deployed to staging cluster at 2026-03-21T09:12Z.
ajosh: Latency numbers? p95 and throughput?
anika: p95 is ~18% faster on int4 for our 4-stream batch profile, p99 increases by ~6% under 80% CPU load. Throughput per GPU up 2.6x.
maya: From a product POV GTN will want a clear recommendation: when to trade cost for accuracy. Maybe route retrieval-heavy queries to int8 or a mitigated int4 variant?
li: Suggest hybrid mitigation: keep attention key/value in int8, or apply per-layer FP16 for top-4 transformer layers. Small config I tried improved citation accuracy by ~5.3pt.
carla: Experiment config I used:
```
model: helios-12b
quant: int4
kv_dtype: int8_prefix<=256
fp16_layers: top_k=4
```
Result: citation drop reduced from -9.2% -> -3.9%.
ajosh: Econ calc: int8 cost = $0.000006/token (baseline). int4 gives 3.1x reduction -> $0.000001935/token. If we route 25% traffic to int8 (retrieval-heavy) and 75% to hybrid int4, weighted cost = 0.75*0.000001935 + 0.25*0.000006 = ~$0.0000026/token.
anika: That's compelling. But GTN wants per-session delta and expected cost uplift for heavy-retrieval customers. We should compute per-session expected cost for avg session length 900 tokens.
maya: Also need a signal for routing: rely on upstream tagging (search-query, retrieval=true) + heuristic classifier (predicts retrieval_dependency >0.6).
li: Propose routing policy: if retrieval_score > 0.6 or session_length > 600 -> use int8; else use helios-int4-hybrid. Add a fallback to int8 when citation_fidelity drops >5% in rolling window.
carla: A/B plan: 5k sessions for 72h, monitor citation precision/recall, hallucination rate, latency, and cost. Use bootstrapped CI.
ajosh: We should prepare a one-slide scorecard for GTN comparing: pure int8, pure int4, and hybrid. Include per-token cost, delta on citation slice, and recommended routing rule.
anika: Quick numbers for the slide:
- pure int8: cost $0.000006/token, citation baseline (0% delta), latency p95 baseline
- pure int4: cost $0.000001935/token, citation -9.2%
- hybrid (75% int4-hybrid / 25% int8): cost ~$0.0000026/token, citation -1.8% (modeled)
We should highlight that hybrid recovers most accuracy while keeping ~57% unit-cost savings vs pure int8.
maya: Also flag operational caveats: mixed-precision KV can increase memory pressure and impacts batching; require batch_compat checks and a health metric for kv-coherence failures.
li: Add canary flags for ops:
```
--routing.retrieval_threshold=0.6
--model.helios-12b.int4.hybrid_kv=true
--model.helios-12b.int4.fp16_top_layers=4
--fallback=helios-12b-int8
--canary=5
```
carla: I'll run the 72h A/B and produce the detailed scorecard. Need help instrumenting the hallucination classifier on staging (maya?).
maya: On it. I'll also produce the threshold ROC so product can pick an operating point.
ajosh: Action items:
- anika: draft GTN slide + unit-econ calc (today)
- carla: run 72h A/B on 5k retrieval sessions (start now)
- maya: instrument hallucination and retrieval classifier on staging
- li: push hybrid_kv + fp16-top-layers canary config and add batch_compat guard
- infra-bot: monitor p99 tail and kv-memory growth over canary window
anika: If A/B results show citation delta <=3% and latency within SLO, recommend default hybrid routing by retrieval_score. Otherwise keep int8 for retrieval flows.
maya: Sounds good. I'll post interim QA logs in this thread. :mag:
anika: Thanks everyone. We'll sync results in 48h and finalize GTN recommendation. :rocket:
